newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian employers see lower production in May.
newsitem.headline: Italian employers see lower production in May.

text.p: Italian employers' federation Confindustria said industrial production was set to fall 2.1 percent in May from the same month in 1996 but average daily output was higher because one day less had been worked.
Confindustria said in a statement that average daily production was forecast to rise 1.9 percent. There are 21 working days in May this year against 22 in May 1996.
The average daily index, seasonally adjusted, is set to rise 0.4 percent. The index is forecast to rise 0.8 percent in the first five months of the year over the year earlier period.
New orders were seen rising 3.7 percent in May year-on-year with sales of manufactures up 1.3 percent.
